AbstractText.Label: INTRODUCTION
AbstractText.content: Since the development of distal chip endoscopes with a working channel, diagnostic and therapeutic possibilities in the outpatient clinic in the management of laryngeal pathology have increased. Which of these office-based procedures are currently available, and their clinical indications and possible advantages, remains unclear.

AbstractText.Label: MATERIAL AND METHODS
AbstractText.content: Review of literature on office-based procedures in laryngology and head and neck oncology.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Flexible endoscopic biopsy (FEB), vocal cord injection, and laser surgery are well-established office-based procedures that can be performed under topical anesthesia. These procedures demonstrate good patient tolerability and multiple advantages.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Office-based procedures under topical anesthesia are currently an established method in the management of laryngeal pathology. These procedures offer medical and economic advantages compared with operating room-performed procedures. Furthermore, office-based procedures enhance the speed and timing of the diagnostic and therapeutic process.
